three-stages.title: Three stages
three-stages.keywords: leads, opportunities, closing, stranger to customer, three words
three-stages.script: A sale has three stages, from left to right. Leads, opportunities, and closing. Each one is a different kind of work. Someone is a stranger, then a name on your list, then a conversation, then a customer. The stages are only names for where a person is on that way. Keep these three words, because the rest of this part uses them.

leads.title: Leads
leads.keywords: second action, spreadsheet, ten names today, every week, company, person, why they care
leads.script: Start with leads. A lead is simply the name of someone who might buy. Research them and keep a list. This is your second action, and you can do it today. Open a spreadsheet, add ten names, and keep adding them every week. Do not make the list perfect. Write down the company, the person, and why you think they might care. If you do not know yet, write down a guess, and fix it after the first call. The only wrong list is the empty one.

first-contact.title: First contact
first-contact.keywords: third action, cold call, inbound, network, short honest message, a no teaches for free
first-contact.script: Then comes first contact. You can cold call, you can answer someone who came to you, or you can ask your network. Pick the one you are least afraid of and begin. This is your third action. Each conversation that goes somewhere turns a lead into an opportunity. Many people fear that they are bothering others. A short, honest message is a fair thing to send. And if they say no, you have learned something for free.

opportunities.title: Opportunities
opportunities.keywords: the real work, conversations, questions, proposal, most of your week, steady lead research
opportunities.script: Opportunities are where the real work lives. Conversations, questions, a proposal. If you spend all your time on lead research, you are researching, not selling. At some point a name has to become a conversation, and a conversation has to become a proposal. Put most of your week into the opportunities you already have. Keep a small, steady part for adding new names to the lead stage.

after-closing.title: After closing
after-closing.keywords: signature, delivery, more waiting, revenue after signature, zero-cash month earlier
after-closing.script: Closing is not the end of the story for your cash. After the signature comes the delivery, and delivery is more waiting. Your revenue lands later than your signature, so count that gap into your board. How long does delivery take in your business? A week? A quarter? Add it to the board as a note after the signature, and you will find your zero-cash month a little earlier than you thought.
